subject: Annual commit tiers — phased ramp + overage safeguard proposal
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Elena Torres <elena@brightwave.ai>, BrightWave Procurement <procurement@brightwave.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Jan 2026 16:15:00 +0000
Subject: Annual commit tiers — initial proposal and phased ramp idea

Hi Elena / team,

Thanks for the time yesterday — really excited about the BrightWave use case for document summarization and the timing you outlined. Attached is a concise annual commit proposal that maps to the Starter / Growth / Enterprise tiers we discussed plus a phased ramp option to reduce upfront risk. High-level: 

- Starter: 200M tokens/year — $0.0009 per token list, 5% discount on first-year actuals if >80% utilization.
- Growth: 1.2B tokens/year — $0.0007 per token list, 12% effective discount with smoothing credits.
- Enterprise: 6B tokens/year — $0.00045 per token list, 20% committed discount + priority routing.

Phased ramp (new): we split the Growth and Enterprise commits into 3 quarters of stepped target consumption with a smoothing credit pool to cover early ramp overshoot. Key safeguards:
- Carry-forward credits up to 10% of committed tokens per quarter.
- Overage capped at 125% of quarterly target; over that, overage rate = list * 0.95 (i.e., small premium vs. committed rate).
- If you under-utilize in Q1/Q2, smoothing credits can be applied to Q3 to avoid double-charging.

Attachments: BrightWave_Annual_Commit_Proposal_Q1-2026.pdf, commit_tier_ramp_table.xlsx

If the above looks reasonable, next steps we propose: 1) confirm target tier, 2) agree ramp schedule, 3) sign SOW + start onboarding. Happy to run numbers on a 12-month cash vs smoothing model if finance wants.

Best,
Marissa

Subject: Re: Annual commit tiers — initial proposal and phased ramp idea

Thanks Marissa — this is helpful. A couple of items from procurement/finance we need clarified before we can move to signature: 

1) Smoothing mechanics: can smoothing credits be applied retroactively if we undershoot early in the year? We need to avoid a scenario where early months look low and we get penalized immediately.
2) Overage cap: 125% per quarter is sensible, but procurement is asking for a true hard cap on spend exposure (i.e., stop-charge threshold) — can we agree on a dollar-based stop-charge for accidental spikes?
3) Ramp pause: BrightWave plans a limited pilot in Q1; we may want to pause ramp if pilot shows different token economics. Is a one-time pause allowed without a penalty?

Also attaching a short procurement checklist we use — you'll see we prefer clear carry-forward rules and an explicit annual reconciliation.

Subject: Re: Annual commit tiers — initial proposal and phased ramp idea

Marissa — quick internal note / proposed responses to procurement asks: 

- Smoothing retroactivity: we can allow retroactive application of smoothing credits within the same billing year, but cap retro-applied credits to 15% of annual committed tokens to prevent gaming.
- Dollar stop-charge: propose a per-quarter stop-charge of $75k for Growth tier and $250k for Enterprise tier. Once the stop-charge is hit, traffic is routed to a lower-cost fallback model until procurement confirms continuation.
- One-time ramp pause: allow one one-month pause within first two quarters without penalty; additional pauses convert to a proportional credit adjustment (i.e., pro-rate commit).

If you want, I can run the modeled cash impact for BrightWave's top-of-funnel ramp (assume 40% of commit in Q1 pilot, 70% in Q2, full in Q3). Also recommend we offer a modest onboarding credit ($12k) for the Growth tier to offset integration work — offsets first invoice.

Rishi
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Elena Torres <elena@brightwave.ai>, BrightWave Procurement <procurement@brightwave.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 16 Jan 2026 13:02:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Annual commit tiers — phased ramp final offer and next steps

Elena — thanks for the clear asks. We spoke internally and can do the following as a good-faith final offer: 

1) Smoothing retroactivity: allowed within the billing year, capped at 15% of committed tokens.
2) Dollar stop-charge: Growth = $75,000 / quarter, Enterprise = $250,000 / quarter. After stop-charge is hit, we route excess to a compatible lower-cost model and pause billing on the committed rate until procurement confirms continuation.
3) One-time ramp pause: one 30-day pause allowed in the first half of the year without penalty. Any additional pauses trigger proportional commit adjustments.
4) Onboarding credit: $12,000 applied to first invoice for Growth tier sign-ups.

I've attached the updated proposal that reflects these points and a simplified quarterly ramp table so finance can see exposure by month. If accepted, we'll push the SOW to DocuSign (link below) and schedule a 90-minute onboarding plan with Solutions Engineering.

DocuSign (proposal): https://www.docusign.com/unsigned/RDW-2026-BW-045

- We: issue quote and DocuSign SOW once confirmed.

Thanks — ready to move quickly.
